capabilities: Draw a due note into a sidebar panel for review
Score recall from 0 to 5 to move the note along an editable interval ladder
Balance draws across folders and spend an explore rate on never-reviewed notes
Store review progress as sr-* fields in note frontmatter or a plugin data file
Draw from the same review pool via a command-line version for AI assistants
extras: Free with no account or telemetry; the interface ships in English and Simplified Chinese; a standalone CLI companion (skills/spaced-dive/) shares the same picking rules and progress data without needing Obsidian running. The manifest notes the plugin has not been manually reviewed by Obsidian staff.
motivation: The author built it for vaults written over years and rarely reopened, because card-based plugins put all the work at the beginning and all the payoff at the end.
problem: Card-based spaced-repetition plugins require carving notes into question-and-answer pairs up front, and that upfront work makes most people quit before seeing the payoff.

relations.evidence: renaming a note orphans its record, and Dataview can't see it
There's also a command-line version for AI assistants — Claude Code, WorkBuddy, and similar

summary: Spaced-repetition tool that reviews whole notes on a forgetting curve: it draws a note, you read and score it 0-5, and the score sets the next interval.
